title: Cloud Agent release manifest
description: One Cloud Agent release: the commit it was built from, every artifact the deployment must run, pinned by digest, and what those artifacts claim about themselves. Written by deploy/release/release_manifest.py. FreeInference pins the sha256 of this document's bytes and nothing else, so the fields here are the whole contract between the two repositories.

schema_version.description: Manifest format version. A consumer that does not know this number must refuse the document rather than guess.

source_repository.description: The repository whose commit produced every artifact below.

source_commit.description: Full 40-hex commit. Must equal the org.opencontainers.image.revision label of every platform image in every artifact, which is what a resolver checks against the registry rather than taking this document's word for it.

deploy_protocol.description: The deployment protocol these artifacts require, read from deploy/DEPLOY_PROTOCOL rather than typed. A deployer that does not implement it must refuse the release; an application rollback must not carry an old deployer back with it.

artifacts.description: Every image the deployment runs: exactly one entry per role, and web exactly one per build variant because basePath is resolved at build time. A release is not consumable until all of them exist: a missing artifact is not a smaller release, it is a broken one, and a list of the right length holding the wrong roles is the same failure wearing a valid-looking shape. The cardinality is enforced with contains/minContains/maxContains per role rather than by counting entries.

runtime_catalog.description: The Agent CLIs the sandbox image actually contains, read from that image's own org.freeinference.runtime.* labels rather than from Dockerfile defaults — the labels are derived from the effective build arguments and cross-checked against the installed binaries at build time.

database_revision.description: The Alembic revision this release migrates to, derived from migrations/versions rather than typed. A preflight compares it with the database it is about to migrate.

publisher_run_url.description: The trusted workflow run that built and published this release, so the document points at the process that produced it rather than at whoever handed it over.

role.description: What the image is for. Verified against the image's own io.hybridinference.artifact.role label, not against the registry path: which package or tag an image lives in is storage layout, and a deployment must not depend on it.

variant.description: Web only. The build variant, implied by basePath.

base_path.description: Web only. The prefix the app is built to serve under, which is a property of the image rather than of the deployment.

image.description: A full digest reference. Tags may exist for humans; nothing selects on one.

platforms.description: The platforms this artifact was built and started on. Declared per artifact: a single-platform image is not a multi-architecture one, and the resolver verifies the index really carries them.

default.description: The version a session runs when it does not ask for one. Must appear in versions.

versions.description: Every version installed in the sandbox, default first, in the order the image declares them.

recipe.description: The generic deployment recipe: Compose files, protocol files and host helpers, archived so a deployment can be prepared without a source checkout.

url.description: Where the archive is fetched from. A release asset, so it is immutable once published.

format_version.description: Recipe layout version, so a deployer can refuse a recipe it does not know how to use.

compatibility.description: What this release has actually been exercised against. Deliberately not inferred from the Alembic revision: a schema that is backwards compatible says nothing about whether a rollback was rehearsed.

minimum_deployer.description: The deployment protocol a deployer must implement to install this release.

verified_upgrade_from.description: Source commits this release has been upgraded from in an acceptance run. Empty means none has been.

verified_rollback_to.description: Source commits this release has been rolled back to in an acceptance run. Empty means none has been, and a deployment must not assume otherwise.
